body:
Path-gradient propagation repeats terrain-cost and admission checks in its eight-neighbor loop. This specializes uniform-cost movement, reads the weighted terrain cost once per settled cell, and replaces the relaxation checks with an equivalent unsigned range comparison. Queue order, distance values, cost caps, and simulation behavior are preserved.

The diff contains only the kernel and focused regression coverage: an independent heap-Dijkstra oracle linked to the real Map implementation, its SCons target, and execution in Linux/Windows CI. No profiling flags, repair/cache experiments, reports, binaries, or generated artifacts are included.

### Validation

- Real-engine oracle: 1,526 cases / 2,032,787 exact cell comparisons. Covers all seven movement classes, intermediate seeds, cap/sentinel boundaries, water boundaries, thin/wrapped maps, and shared-scratch reuse. Output digest: `3281260807785418242`.
- Extracted production-kernel differential/oracle checks: ARM64 optimized, ARM64 ASan/UBSan, and x86_64 execution under Rosetta; identical outputs in all three configurations.
- Building invalidation, immobile occupancy, clearing, resource-fetch, round-trip hunger, and save-safety harnesses pass locally.
- Existing cross-platform checksum fixtures pass on macOS ARM64, Linux GCC 11, Linux GCC 13, and Windows MinGW: 3,072 original-game ticks plus 256 checkpoint-continuation ticks. All seven [CI jobs](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/35412143952) passed, including the new production-linked oracle on both Linux configurations and Windows.
- Mature fresh-process reload: original and candidate match on all 250 resumed ticks. Both reproduce the existing baseline interruption-versus-reload divergence at tick 30252; this change does not fix that independent issue.

Reproduce the new regression with `scons release=1 server=0 path-gradient-test` and `build/src/PathGradientHarness` (`.exe` on Windows). Simulation fixture check: `python3 test/check_telemetry_simulation.py build/src/glob2`.

### Sampling evidence

Separate equal-input paired sampling on macOS ARM64 compared 55,860 complete Uint16 fields, with zero differences. Solvers alternate execution order within each movement class; seed cloning and output comparison are outside the sampled solver frames. Requested interval: 2 ms. These are sampled solver-work estimates, not whole-engine speedup percentages.

| 256×256 / eight-player checkpoint | Original observations | Optimized observations | Optimized/original |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Isles / mixed AIs | 14,348 | 11,859 | 0.827 |
| Maze / mixed AIs | 4,434 | 3,722 | 0.839 |
| Everglades / Maxima | 3,128 | 2,410 | 0.770 |

All three map aggregates favor the candidate in both execution orders. Profiles resume baseline `326c05fda` checkpoints at tick 30000 and run to tick 33000. Generator/map-seed/game-seed: Isles `6/111/2005`, Maze `11/121/2009`, Everglades `19/131/2015`; dimensions use `--param width=8 --param height=8 --param teams=8`. Shared-host scheduling, correlated samples, and cache warming limit precise speedup inference. The paired measurement machinery remains outside this PR.

### Wider map validation (macOS ARM64)

The actual PR binary and baseline `326c05fda` each loaded the same baseline-generated tick-zero saves. All **16 games × 3,000 ticks = 48,000 detailed tick records** matched, including byte-for-byte equality of the complete checksum streams and all tick indices 0–2999. All games reached the tick cap with eight AI controllers: Castor, Warrush, Econo, Nicowar, Cortex, Maxima, Cabino, Numbi.

| Actual dimensions | Arena (dry/open) | Maze | Isles | Everglades |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64×64 | Rejected setup | Rejected setup | 1/1 pass | Rejected setup |
| 128×128 | 2/2 pass | 2/2 pass | 1/1 pass | 2/2 pass |
| 256×256 | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass |
| 512×512 | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass | 1/1 pass |

The tested eight-player 64×64 arena, maze, and wetland setups were rejected by their generators. Those seeds were rerun at 128×128; this is **13 distinct size/type combinations plus three extra 128×128 seeds**, not a complete 4×4 grid. This adds early-game coverage on macOS ARM64; the earlier mature-game and cross-platform tests remain separate evidence.

<details>
<summary>Seeds and reproduction commands</summary>

| Dimensions | Generator ID | Map seed | Game seed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 128×128 | 15 | 64015 | 164015 |
| 128×128 | 11 | 64011 | 164011 |
| 64×64 | 6 | 64006 | 164006 |
| 128×128 | 19 | 64019 | 164019 |
| 128×128 | 15 | 128015 | 228015 |
| 128×128 | 11 | 128011 | 228011 |
| 128×128 | 6 | 128006 | 228006 |
| 128×128 | 19 | 128019 | 228019 |
| 256×256 | 15 | 256015 | 356015 |
| 256×256 | 11 | 256011 | 356011 |
| 256×256 | 6 | 256006 | 356006 |
| 256×256 | 19 | 256019 | 356019 |
| 512×512 | 15 | 512015 | 612015 |
| 512×512 | 11 | 512011 | 612011 |
| 512×512 | 6 | 512006 | 612006 |
| 512×512 | 19 | 512019 | 612019 |

IDs: arena=15, maze=11, Isles=6, Everglades=19. Arena uses `--param moat=0 --param lakes=0`; other settings are generator defaults at the baseline commit. Width/height arguments are powers of two: 64→6, 128→7, 256→8, 512→9. Example for the 128×128 maze:

```sh
BASELINE --run-game --generator 11 --map-seed 128011 \
  --param width=7 --param height=7 --param teams=8 --game-seed 228011 \
  --player castor --player warrush --player econo --player nicowar \
  --player cortex --player maxima --player cabino --player numbi \
  --ticks 1 --save initial --output-dir fixture
BASELINE --run-game --load-game fixture/initial.game --ticks 3000 \
  --save final --replay true --telemetry checksums --output-dir baseline-run
CANDIDATE --run-game --load-game fixture/initial.game --ticks 3000 \
  --save final --replay true --telemetry checksums --output-dir candidate-run
cmp baseline-run/game.replay.checksums candidate-run/game.replay.checksums
```

`BASELINE` is built from `326c05fda`; `CANDIDATE` from `4b0a91a299`. Retained inputs, outputs, commands and binary hashes are stored outside Git. No generated evidence or extra source files were added to this PR.

</details>

### Wider paired sampling (macOS ARM64)

Using the matching tick-3,000 baseline saves above, a separate measurement binary ran both kernels on identical field inputs, alternating execution order per movement class. **27,780 complete fields matched exactly**, with zero mismatches. Native stack sampling used a requested 2 ms interval; cloning and comparison were outside solver frames. No wall-time ranking is used.

| Size | Map | Tick window | Original observations | Optimized observations | Optimized/original |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 128×128 | everglades | 3000–6000 | 222 | 124 | 0.559 |
| 128×128 | isles | 3000–6000 | 340 | 228 | 0.671 |
| 128×128 | maze | 3000–6000 | 194 | 166 | 0.856 |
| 128×128 | symmetric-arena | 3000–6000 | 191 | 151 | 0.791 |
| 512×512 | everglades | 3000–4000 | 844 | 520 | 0.616 |
| 512×512 | isles | 3000–4000 | 602 | 505 | 0.839 |
| 512×512 | maze | 3000–4000 | 913 | 715 | 0.783 |
| 512×512 | symmetric-arena | 3000–4000 | 468 | 338 | 0.722 |

All eight map aggregates favored the candidate in both execution orders. These are **sampled solver-work ratios, not whole-engine CPU reductions**. The 128×128 cases have only 191–340 original observations each, so their estimates remain coarse. Short overlapping 128×128 pilots were extended once for sample count and excluded from this table.

Coverage is predominantly uniform-cost class 0 (25,215 of 27,780 calls). Classes 1/2 did not occur; class 3 had only one original observation and class 6 none. This expansion does **not** establish a benefit for every weighted movement class. Host load, correlated/descheduled samples, instrumentation and cache warming remain limitations. These early-game results are separate from the mature 256×256 sampling above.

Sampling used the standard 128/512 seeds in the table above, starting from `baseline-run/final.game`, with `--ticks 6000` for 128 or `--ticks 4000` for 512, `--replay false`, and no checksum telemetry or saves. Native capture: `/usr/bin/sample PID 30 2 -file sample.txt`; counts include only named original/optimized solver frames. The paired measurement binary and generated evidence remain outside the PR.
title: Optimize path gradient propagation with exact regression coverage
